info.bio:
Andre Hicks (July 5, 1970 - November 1, 2004), better known by his stage name, Mac Dre, was a Bay Area based gangsta rapper from the Crest side of Vallejo, California, active since 1988 and considered one of the predecessors of the hyphy movement. During his career in the rap world, he worked with artists like Andre Nickatina, Yukmouth, Snoop Dogg, Mac Mall, Dubee and Keak da Sneak.

Career

Mac Dre's music gained popularity in the early to mid 1990s throughout the Bay Area

scenes.name: Mac Dre, E-40 y el hyphy
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Andre Hicks, Mac Dre, se dio a conocer en el instituto con «Too Hard for the Fuckin’ Radio»; la policía de Vallejo, a la que criticaba, usó sus letras contra él y en 1992 aceptó cinco años por una conspiración de atraco en Fresno en la que apenas tuvo que ver, sin delatar a nadie; grabó Back n da Hood por teléfono desde la cárcel. Al salir fundó Thizz Entertainment en Sacramento y llevó la fiesta a toda la bahía: el hyphy (palabra de Keak Da Sneak), bajos martilleantes, baile frenético y «ghost riding». Lo mataron a tiros en Kansas City en 2004 y su muerte sigue sin resolver: el rey de la bahía. En 2006 el hyphy llegó al país con My Ghetto Report Card de E-40, Mistah F.A.B., Too $hort y Keak Da Sneak; para Mac Mall, la etiqueta acabó haciendo que todo sonara igual.

mentions.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
mentions.author: Jonathan Abrams
mentions.text: ANDRE HICKS WAS born in Oakland before moving to the Vallejo area and assuming the stage name Mac Dre. In high school, he first gained attention for a cassette tape that featured the single “Too Hard for the Fuckin’ Radio.” In the early 1990s, law enforcement began focusing on the Vallejo area. Mac Dre, who was vocal about the police department infringing on the rights of citizens, came under scrutiny by law enforcement officials, who attempted to use his lyrics as evidence against him.
